nil.h: Show him the money: the 10 biggest NIL raises of the offseason
nil.d: $1000K in new money across the top 10, and two of them changed schools to get it. Nobody got a bigger bump than [[p:557721034|N.Sheppard]]: 620K to 720K.

list.name: N.Sheppard
list.d: [[t:832438312|Georgia]] wasn't letting him walk. Last season: 209 rushing yards, 3 TD. Up 4 overall since the end of last season (92 to 96).

list.name: D.Lee Jr.
list.d: [[t:832438357|Notre Dame]] wasn't letting him walk. Last season: 10 tackles, 1 INT.

list.name: C.Peal
list.d: [[t:832438380|Syracuse]] paid up to keep him. Last season: 24 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 2 INT. Up 5 overall since the end of last season (87 to 92).

list.name: K.Minchey
list.d: Re-signed with [[t:832438319|Indiana]] on a much bigger number. Last season: 610 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT. Up 4 overall since the end of last season (81 to 85).

list.name: J.Braxton
list.d: Followed the money through the portal from [[t:832438373|San Diego State]] to [[t:832438288|BYU]]. Last season: 18 tackles, 1 INT.

list.name: K.Bolden
list.d: Re-signed with [[t:832438312|Georgia]] on a much bigger number. Last season: 10 tackles. Up 5 overall since the end of last season (87 to 92).

list.name: J.Gilchrist
list.d: Re-signed with [[t:832438281|Auburn]] on a much bigger number. Last season: 3 games.

list.name: B.Bentley
list.d: [[t:832438333|LSU]] paid up to keep him. Up 3 overall since the end of last season (83 to 86).

list.name: J.Daulton
list.d: Cashed in on the portal, trading [[t:832438338|Miami University]] for [[t:832438385|Texas A&M]].

list.name: J.Hardy
list.d: [[t:832438317|Houston]] paid up to keep him. Last season: 22 tackles. Up 6 overall since the end of last season (72 to 78).

breakouts.h: Breakout watch: 12 players ready to make the leap
breakouts.d: Rating jumps from offseason training, new starting jobs, scheme fits and what they did with limited snaps last year. These are the names to know before kickoff.

list.name: B.Jackson
list.d: [[p:557716657|B.Jackson]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. On top of that, came out of the offseason at 93 overall, up from 89, and his speed (88 to 92) and ball security (83 to 87) took a big step. By October, everyone will know it.

list.name: F.Brewu
list.d: [[p:557712705|F.Brewu]] came out of the offseason at 91 overall, up from 85. Better yet, his tackling (80 to 88) and strength (76 to 84) took a big step, and is penciled in as a starter for the first time. Don't be surprised to see him on an all-conference team.

list.name: G.Davidson
list.d: [[p:557714033|G.Davidson]] came out of the offseason at 90 overall, up from 85. On top of that, his ball security (69 to 77) and juke move (86 to 93) took a big step, and landed at [[t:832438293|Clemson]] through the portal and walks into a starting job. Clemson fans are about to get a new favorite player.

list.name: B.Eskildsen
list.d: [[p:557714640|B.Eskildsen]] his deep route running (70 to 77) and spectacular-catch ability (76 to 83) took a big step. Better yet, came out of the offseason at 88 overall, up from 84, and Penn State threw it more than almost anyone last year (7th in passing yards per game). Don't be surprised to see him on an all-conference team.

list.name: K.Pepe
list.d: [[p:557725754|K.Pepe]] came out of the offseason at 85 overall, up from 79. Better yet, his run blocking (75 to 83) and awareness (79 to 87) took a big step, and is penciled in as a starter for the first time. This is the year.

list.name: B.Jackson II
list.d: [[p:557716642|B.Jackson II]] came out of the offseason at 86 overall, up from 80. Add this: his acceleration (81 to 89) and vision (83 to 91) took a big step, and Wisconsin leans on the run game (5th in rushing yards per game last year). Circle his name now.

list.name: J.Walton
list.d: [[p:557726572|J.Walton]] jumped from 84 to 90 overall this offseason. Better yet, his trucking (79 to 87) and hands (71 to 78) took a big step, and he ran for 5.8 yards a carry as a backup. Don't be surprised to see him on an all-conference team.

list.name: D.Sanchez
list.d: [[p:557720766|D.Sanchez]] is penciled in as a starter for the first time. On top of that, his agility (93 to 99) and hands (75 to 81) took a big step, and came out of the offseason at 92 overall, up from 89. This is the year.

list.name: J.Patterson
list.d: [[p:557719653|J.Patterson]] jumped from 78 to 84 overall this offseason. Better yet, his speed (82 to 90) and acceleration (84 to 92) took a big step, and Rice leans on the run game (18th in rushing yards per game last year). Don't be surprised to see him on an all-conference team.

list.name: D.Murph
list.d: [[p:557719119|D.Murph]] came out of the offseason at 87 overall, up from 81. Better yet, landed at [[t:832438377|South Carolina]] through the portal and walks into a starting job, and South Carolina threw it more than almost anyone last year (8th in passing yards per game). South Carolina fans are about to get a new favorite player.

list.name: T.Gentry
list.d: [[p:557724537|T.Gentry]] came out of the offseason at 85 overall, up from 80. On top of that, slides into the starting lineup with J.Koger gone, and Texas Tech threw it more than almost anyone last year (2nd in passing yards per game). Circle his name now.

list.name: M.Ford
list.d: [[p:557714967|M.Ford]] came out of the offseason at 86 overall, up from 80. Add this: his vision (80 to 87) and hands (68 to 75) took a big step, and is penciled in as a starter for the first time. By October, everyone will know it.
